library.name: EspBle
library.author: TANAKA Masayuki
library.sentence: General-purpose Bluetooth Low Energy library for ESP32 Arduino.
library.paragraph: EspBle talks to the NimBLE host bundled with Arduino-ESP32 directly, without the bundled BLE wrapper classes. It provides central and peripheral roles with multiple simultaneous connections, generic GATT client and server operations addressable by UUID or attribute handle, pairing and bonding, standard GATT services, and composable profiles: HID device and host (keyboard, mouse, consumer and system control, gamepad, vendor and fully custom reports) plus BLE MIDI device and host. On the original ESP32, whose prebuilt libraries are built with Bluedroid, EspBle bundles its own NimBLE host; that chip has a BLE 4.2 controller, so some features are unavailable and behaviour may differ slightly. That chip also gets Bluetooth Classic, through a separately built, namespaced Bluedroid host: SPP as a byte stream or an Arduino Stream, HID device and host with the same API as the BLE side, A2DP and AVRCP, and HFP client and audio gateway, all carrying already-encoded audio payloads. Which Classic features are hardware-verified, unverified or unimplemented is documented in the repository.

library.name: SnappyXOShield
library.author: SnappyXO
library.sentence: Motor control library for the SnappyXO Motor Shield v2 and v3, with optional encoder motors.
library.paragraph: Knows the shield's motor pins and drives a two-wheeled robot: forward, reverse, spins, each wheel's speed, joystick-style drive(throttle, steering), stop and brake. With encoder motors: how far and how fast each wheel turns, driving a set distance in inches or centimeters, and turning by an angle.

library.name: WisBlockLoRaWAN
library.author: Bernd Giesecke bernd@giesecke.tk
library.sentence: Unified LoRaWAN (Class A/B/C) and LoRa P2P library for RAKwireless WisBlock boards using Semtech SX1262 + LoRa Basics Modem.
library.paragraph: Supports RAK4631 (nRF52840), RAK3312 (ESP32-S3) and RAK11310/RAK11300 (RP2040, Arduino-Pico core by Earle Philhower) with built-in SX1262. Provides AT command interface and C++ API. LoRaWAN engine is built on Semtech's LoRa Basics Modem (Basics Modem/LBM) stack.
